name: PakTech
old_description: Since 2012, PakTech has repurposed over half a billion gallon-sized milk jugs into new packaging handles, keeping roughly 80 million pounds out of the waste stream. Manufacturing our products with 100% recycled and recyclable material generates 78% less greenhouse gases, uses 90% less energy, and reduces virgin petroleum production by 100%. And after they’ve been used, PakTech handles can be recycled again – we’ve partnered with more than 500 businesses to establish dedicated recycling sites, so our handles can live again as park benches, planter pots, and new PakTech products.
about:
PakTech is headquartered in Eugene, Oregon. The family-owned company was founded in 1991, originally operating as a job shop producing molds for injection-molding firms before pivoting to manufacturing its own injection-molded handles from recycled HDPE for the beverage industry.

Today PakTech designs and manufactures 100% recyclable multi-pack handles and automated in-line application equipment. The handles are injection molded from 100% post-consumer recycled HDPE, sourced from materials such as milk jugs. The company also supplies the applicators that integrate into packaging lines for high-speed multi-packing.

PakTech serves the food, beverage, and consumer goods sectors, including household products. Its handles are used to multi-pack soft drinks, beer, wine, cider, kombucha, craft cocktails, coffee, juice, water, cleaning supplies, and health and beauty items. Customers range from established corporations to start-up manufacturers.

The company was built on a commitment to environmentally friendly manufacturing, using 100% recycled and recyclable HDPE to reduce waste and greenhouse gas emissions. Its mission emphasizes smart, low-waste packaging handles, turnkey automated equipment, superior product quality, customer service, and long-term partnerships. PakTech's recycled content is certified by SCS Global Services, and it has established recycling partnerships with over 500 businesses to keep handles in a circular loop.
